It does not test an intensive systolic blood pressure target (<120 mmHg) versus a standard target as an intervention arm (the hypothesized mechanism pertains specifically to treatment effect modification by an intensive BP-target intervention such as in SPRINT). Although SBP is analyzed and predicts outcomes, the study assesses SBP as a baseline prognostic marker in a stroke population receiving DAPT rather than whether an intensive SBP treatment strategy alters absolute treatment benefit for major cardiovascular events or all-cause mortality. Therefore it fails the intervention-match gate and is not relevant to the proposed mechanism.
abstracts_analyzed.evidence_quote: After IPW, patients with admission SBP ⩾124 mm Hg versus <124 mm Hg had a significantly higher risk of 90-day ischemic stroke or other vascular events (adjusted HR: 2.14 (95% CI 1.07%-4.98%); p = 0.033). Subgroup analysis showed a significant interaction between admission SBP, sex, and time to DAPT start in predicting 90-day new vascular events (p for interaction <0.001 and 0.007, respectively).
abstracts_analyzed.title: Admission systolic blood pressure and short-term outcomes after dual antiplatelet therapy in patients with minor ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack.

abstracts_analyzed.reasoning: Although the trial intervention (intensive vs standard SBP target) and outcomes (cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality) match the trial context, the abstract does not analyze or report subgroup effects by the TARGET FEATURE (Sbp). Instead, the analysis stratifies participants by baseline diastolic blood pressure (DBP) and hs-cTnT. Because the mechanism to be tested specifically concerns baseline systolic blood pressure (Sbp) modifying absolute treatment benefit, the absence of any SBP-based subgroup or interaction analysis means the abstract cannot provide evidence for or against the proposed Sbp-related mechanism. The study is a nonprespecified subgroup analysis of SPRINT (an RCT), so while relevant overall, it is irrelevant for the specific Sbp mechanism.
abstracts_analyzed.evidence_quote: A total of 8828 participants in SPRINT ... were stratified by baseline DBP. Those with low DBP (<70 mm Hg) were further stratified by elevated hs-cTnT (≥14 ng/L) at baseline. Randomization to intensive versus standard BP lowering led to similar reductions in cardiovascular disease risk among individuals with low DBP/high hs-cTnT ..., low DBP/low hs-cTnT ..., and DBP ≥70 mm Hg (P for interaction=0.20).
abstracts_analyzed.title: Intensive Blood Pressure Lowering in Individuals With Low Diastolic Blood Pressure and Elevated Troponin Levels in SPRINT.
